definition: Networks that carry data between places, with their sites and civil works. Includes domestic fibre, submarine cables and international links, mobile and fixed wireless networks and towers, satellite links, government and institutional networks, and last-mile connections to users and institutions, including public Wi-Fi and community networks. Equipment takes the asset of the network it is installed in or connects to; equipment with no network named has no asset. A policy takes this asset only when it names or governs a network on this list, such as tower-siting rules; sector-wide law or strategy has no asset. A security operations centre or security audit for the network, and training or capacity building for it, take this asset; national cybersecurity strategy has none.

Facilities and computing services that host, store or process data and applications. Includes data centres, server rooms, colocation, cloud hosting and computing capacity, their power and cooling, backup and recovery sites, and internet exchange points. A data warehouse or data lake as a storage facility or capacity is hosting; the application or database system on top of it is platforms. Equipment takes the asset of the facility it is installed in; equipment with no facility named has no asset. A policy takes this asset only when it names or governs a facility or service on this list, such as a cloud-hosting rule; sector-wide law or strategy has no asset. A security operations centre or security audit for the data centre, and training or capacity building for it, take this asset; with no facility named, training has no asset.

Software systems and shared digital services, and equipment supplied to run them. Includes digital public infrastructure (identity, civil registration, payments, data exchange, digital signature and trust services), government and sector information systems, registries, service portals and applications, and geospatial data systems. The application or database system on top of a data warehouse or data lake is platforms; the storage facility itself is hosting. Equipment, training and capacity building take the asset of the system they are installed in, connect to or are for; with no system named, they have no asset. A policy takes this asset only when it names or governs a system on this list; sector-wide law or strategy has no asset. A security operations centre, incident response team or security audit for government systems takes this asset; national cybersecurity strategy, law or a national incident response team for the whole sector has none, and cybersecurity itself is not an asset.

Digital systems that sense, monitor, warn about or control the physical world. Includes hydrometeorological and seismic observation networks, forecasting and early warning systems, public alerting and emergency communication systems, and operational technology such as SCADA, smart meters, telemetry, sensor networks and intelligent transport systems. Equipment takes the asset of the system it is installed in or connects to; sensors or equipment with no system named have no asset. A policy takes this asset only when it names or governs a system on this list, such as early-warning protocols; sector-wide law or strategy has no asset. Training and capacity building take the asset they are for; with no system named, none.
